We need propose retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction. Need to find a template that corresponds to carbonyl-ene reaction forward: carbonyl + alkene -> cyclic alcohol (five-membered). So retrosynthesis: break the C-O bond (alcohol) to carbonyl and alkene. The target SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

Let's decode: It's a bicyclic? There's a phenyl attached to an exocyclic alkene? There's a cyclopentanol fused? Actually C@@H1[CH2][CH2][CH2][C@@]1(OH)C(F)(F)F. That's a cyclopentanol with CF3 attached to carbon 15? Wait carbon 15 is attached to CF3 and maybe part of same carbon? The SMILES: ...[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]. So carbon 9 is attached to the cyclopentane ring (positions 9-10-11-12-13). Carbon 13 has OH and attached to carbon 15 which is CF3. So it's a cyclopentanol with CF3 substituent.

Also there is an exocyclic alkene attached to carbon 2 which also attached to phenyl. So overall maybe product of intramolecular carbonyl-ene: starting from a ketone (maybe cyclopentanone with CF3) and an alkene (phenyl-substituted). The ene reaction forms new C-C bond between alkene carbon and carbonyl carbon, forming a new C-O (hydroxyl) at carbonyl carbon, and a new C-C bond between allylic carbon and carbonyl carbon? Actually carbonyl-ene: carbonyl (C=O) reacts with alkene having allylic H; the allylic H transfers to carbonyl oxygen forming OH, and new C-C bond forms between carbonyl carbon and the alkene's terminal carbon (the one bearing the H). So product is an allylic alcohol.

Thus retrosynthesis: break the C-O bond (OH) to carbonyl (C=O) and break the C-C bond formed (between carbonyl carbon and alkene carbon) to regenerate alkene and carbonyl.

We need to find a template ID for carbonyl-ene. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_broken=["alcohol"], functional_groups_formed=["ketone","alkene"]? Actually forward reaction: alcohol formed, ketone broken, alkene formed? In forward carbonyl-ene, ketone + alkene -> allylic alcohol (new C-C bond) and alkene is consumed. So broken: ketone, alkene (C=C). Formed: alcohol, C-C bond. So we can search with functional_groups_broken=["ketone","alkene"], functional_groups_formed=["alcohol"], bonds_formed maybe "C-C". Let's try.
